subject: Observability routing decisions for on-prem VPC — evidence & SIEM mapping
messages:
From: Shawn Kapoor <shawn.kapoor@cygnus-sec.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: alyssa@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — SIEM integration and evidence for private deploy

Jonas — thanks for the quick intro. Acme's security team needs a short, auditable description of what telemetry leaves their VPC for our Redwood Private deployment, and how we map those exports into our SIEM (Splunk). Main asks: 1) list of data types (logs, metrics, traces) and which direction they flow; 2) evidence artifacts that will be delivered for SOC / vendor review (examples: sample logs, connector configs, signed export manifest); 3) confirmation of TLS+mTLS endpoints and any proxy/bastion hops.

Can you surface the team decision on whether we will push using an outbound forwarder from the enclave, or a pull model (Splunk HEC inside their subnet)? We have constraints on egress and a mandated audit trail for everything that leaves the environment.

Appreciate a high-level decision record and what artifacts you can deliver by next Monday.

—Shawn
Cygnus Security (on behalf of Acme)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Shawn Kapoor <shawn.kapoor@cygnus-sec.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, alyssa@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability routing decisions for on-prem VPC — evidence & SIEM mapping

Hi Shawn / Alyssa — thanks, good context. Below is a short decision record and a list of artifacts we will produce. I'll follow up with attachments and a proposed schedule.

Decision summary (short):
- Mode: outbound forwarder (Redwood forwarder running inside customer's VPC enclave) will buffer and publish to Acme's Splunk HEC endpoint over mutual TLS.
- Rationale: preserves customer control of destination, avoids inbound firewall exceptions, and provides an auditable export manifest with per-batch checksums.
- Fallback: if HEC cannot be co-located, we will provide a pull-capable gateway (HEC inside Redwood-managed jump host) but only after written approval and hardened bastion config.

Telemetry accounting (what leaves the VPC):
- Logs: application logs, runtime infra logs (server/stdout/stderr), redwood-serving audit logs (user request metadata, not full prompt content unless customer opts in).
- Metrics: aggregated counters and histograms (no raw token stream), exported at 10s granularity via Prometheus remote-write -> push to splunk metric endpoint.
- Traces: sampled traces with PII redaction; default 1% sample rate, adjustable by policy.

Artifacts we will deliver by Mar 22:
- redwood_obsv_decision_record.pdf (this record + gap analysis)
- evidence_matrix.csv (mapping of artifact -> SOC2 control)
- sample_log_bundle.tar.gz (sanitized samples, pre-signed checksum) — we'll reference this, hosted on Drive link below.
- cert thumbprints and mTLS handshake diagram.

Security notes (short):
- Mutual TLS is required for the HEC endpoint — certs rotated via customer KMS.
- Forwarder maintains signed per-batch manifests and sequence numbers to prevent silent drops.
- All exports are optionally routed through customer's logging proxy; Redwood will not decrypt or persist plaintext outside the forwarder pipeline.

Next steps: Kimberly will validate the audit artifact set. Laura, can you confirm whether Acme prefers a forwarder with syslog over TLS or HEC? Also tagging the engineering runbook owners so we can capture the exact proxy ports.

Thanks,
Jonas
Principal Product Manager — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Shawn Kapoor <shawn.kapoor@cygnus-sec.com>, alyssa@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability routing decisions for on-prem VPC — evidence & SIEM mapping

Jonas — quick validation from security/compliance: the outbound forwarder approach is acceptable if we meet these must-haves. I've annotated the decision record and attached the evidence matrix.

Kimberly's MUST list:
- Forwarder must emit a signed manifest (SHA256) per upload and retain manifests locally for 90 days.
- All trace payloads must have PII fields redacted by the forwarder (we will provide a redaction spec).
- Metrics and logs must be separated in the export pipeline to allow independent retention policies in the SIEM.
- Provide a short runbook for evidence retrieval for audits (who to contact, retention windows, how manifests are verified).

Attachment stubs: [attachment: redwood_obsv_decision_record.pdf (pdf)], [attachment: evidence_matrix.csv (csv)]

Action items assigned: 
- kimberly_park: finalize evidence_matrix and approval checklist (due Mar 19).
- jonas_weber: update decision record with network diagram and manifest schema (due Mar 22).
- laura_bennett: produce runbook snippet for oncall and audit retrieval (due Mar 19).

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Shawn Kapoor <shawn.kapoor@cygnus-sec.com>, alyssa@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability routing decisions for on-prem VPC — evidence & SIEM mapping

All — confirmed. Acme's security preference (per prior call) is an HEC endpoint inside their logging subnet; they will accept the forwarder pushing to that HEC over mTLS. That reduces our need for a bastion.

Draft runbook snippet (excerpt):
- Export path: forwarder -> HEC (10.0.23.10:8088) over mTLS.
- Manifest verification: each batch upload returns 200 + manifest-id; dovetail to their SIEM ingestion ID.
- Audit retrieval: Redwood will surface a pre-signed evidence package (sample logs + manifest + checksum) to the drive link for 90 days. Request flow: security@acmecorp.com -> redwood-evidence@redwood.ai -> attach manifest id.

I'll drop a short network diagram into the Drive folder and finish the runbook by end of day.

—Laura
Solutions Engineering (Private Deploys)
From: Shawn Kapoor <shawn.kapoor@cygnus-sec.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, alyssa@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability routing decisions for on-prem VPC — evidence & SIEM mapping

Perfect — that aligns with Acme's audit requirements. We'll expect the PDF + evidence matrix and the runbook snippet by the dates called out. Once we validate sample bundle and manifest schema, we'll schedule a short cutover test (ingest + manifest verification).

One minor ask from Acme: include a short example of the manifest verification CLI steps so their ops team can replay the check during the test.

Thanks,
Shawn
Cygnus Security (on behalf of Acme)
